content: 1. The United Nations General Assembly report A/67/373, transmitted by the Secretary-General, includes a report from the Director-General of the World Health Organization. This report outlines strategies to enhance and facilitate multisectoral action for the prevention and control of non-communicable diseases through effective partnerships. 2. Barker G. conducted an international literature review and program consultation on adolescents, social support, and help-seeking behavior. The study provides actionable recommendations to address these issues. 3. Devi BC, Tang TS, and Corbex M. conducted a pilot study in Sarawak, Malaysia, demonstrating that clinical downstaging can reduce late-stage presentation of breast and cervical cancer by 50% over four years. The findings were published in the journal Annals of Oncology in 2007. 4. The World Health Organization (WHO) has developed implementation tools, such as the Package of Essential Noncommunicable Disease Interventions (WHO PEN), to support primary healthcare delivery in low-resource settings. 5. The WHO guide on cancer control, specifically focusing on diagnosis and treatment, provides effective programmatic strategies for improving cancer care. 6. The WHO Medical Records Manual serves as a comprehensive guide for developing countries to establish and maintain effective medical record systems. 7. A WHO guide for program managers offers detailed instructions on planning and implementing palliative care services to improve end-of-life care. 8. Gabitova G. and Burke NJ. evaluated a breast cancer patient navigation program in a safety-net setting using mixed methods. Their study highlights the potential for improving healthcare empowerment and was published in BMC Health Services Research in 2014. 9. Ginsburg OM and colleagues developed an mHealth model to increase clinic attendance for breast symptoms in rural Bangladesh. Their study explores how bridging the digital divide can help address disparities in cancer care and was published in The Oncologist in 2014. 10. Wadler BM and colleagues critically reviewed the role of community health workers in improving breast cancer control in South Africa. Their findings were published in Journal of Oncology in 2011. 11. A technical brief for policymakers outlines strategies for designing health financing systems that reduce catastrophic health expenditures, ensuring financial protection for patients. 12. Balogh EP and colleagues summarized an Institute of Medicine workshop on patient-centered cancer treatment planning. The report emphasizes improving the quality of oncology care and was published in The Oncologist in 2011. 13. Young JL authored a guide on hospital-based cancer registries, which is included in the WHO publication Cancer Registration: Principles and Methods. This resource provides essential guidance for establishing cancer registries. 14. Bray F and colleagues published a technical guide through the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) on planning and developing population-based cancer registries in lowand middle-income settings. This publication aims to support cancer surveillance and research efforts.
